notes.note: Uses a literal negative right-hand operand (-2), which is statically detectable. Titan accepts it, so Titan does not implement this check.
The operand is an uninitialized variable, which is generally only detectable at runtime, so the test expects ttcn3verdict:error instead of rejection.

The reference to clause 6.5 (Automatic type) is stale. Tested reading 2: restriction a) of 7.1.0 (operands shall be completely initialized). An uninitialized right-hand operand gives ttcn3verdict:error.
Chosen reading: any type in general. ischosen is excluded because 7.1.8.2 restricts its operand. Covers a representative set of types, not literally every type.
Stopping of evaluation is observed via a side-effecting index function to the right of the failing field reference; its call counter must remain 0.
Tested reading 1: error suppression does not extend to references nested inside an index expression. An omitted-field reference used as index gives ttcn3verdict:error.
Tested the exclusive-restriction reading: ischosen on a record field is rejected.
Tested the reading of EXAMPLE 1: specific value and value list operands are accepted, and an AnyValue union template yields false (not an error).

anytype tests carry a Titan-specific with { extension "anytype ..." } attribute. Titan needs it to populate anytype, and it is legal (tool-specific) per the standard. The same applies to 07.01.08.02_test_003 and _test_005.
